chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man upon whom Zakat became due, and his father died, and there was a debt upon him. Can he pay his Zakat for his father's debt, and for the son there is much wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: If his father had bequeathed him wealth, then a debt manifested upon him which he did not know about at that time, so he can settle it on his behalf, he settles it from all the inheritance and does not settle it from his Zakat. And if he had not bequeathed him wealth, there is no one more deserving of his Zakat than the debt of his father. So when he pays it for his father's debt in this state, it suffices for him.

key_terms.أَوْرَثَهُ: He bequeathed him / He left him as heir

ai.seo_question: How is Zakat paid if a person's father died with debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of debt repayment against Zakat, distinguishing between inherited wealth and personal assets. It establishes that if the father left no estate, the son's Zakat serves as the primary fund to settle the father's debt, reflecting the Shia principle that Zakat is a specific obligation that can be utilized for general debt settlement when no other specific estate is available. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the application of Zakat funds in cases of familial debt.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The Zakāt became due upon the man, and his father died, and upon him was a debt. Can he pay the Zakāt regarding the debt of his father, and for his son there is a lot of wealth?’ So heasws said: ‘If it was so that his father had made him to inherit wealth, then a debt manifested upon him, if he did not know it in that day, so he can fulfil it on his behalf from the entirety of the inheritance, and he should not fulfil it from his Zakāt. And if he did not happen to have inherited wealth, there will not happen to be anything more deserving of his Zakāt than the debts of his father. So when he does pay it regarding the debts of his father, upon this state, he would be suffice from it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that there is a man whose father has died and he is indebted. Can he pay the debts on his father from Zakat he owes when the son has a great wealth? He (the Imam) said, ‘If his father has left a legacy for him and then it is found out that there are debts on his father that he did not know on that day, he pays the debts from the whole legacy, but he does not pay it from his Zakat. However, if he did not leave any legacy then no one is more deserving of his Zakat than the debts of his father. If he pays off the debts of his father in such case it is acceptable (as payment of Zakat).”’
